modules.title: Map the room
modules.summary: Before you write a single email, map who has skin in the game and what shape it takes.
objectives: Identify three categories of stakeholder: decision, influence, blocker
Distinguish power from interest on a 2x2
Spot the stakeholders nobody mentioned but who can still derail you

data.content:
Every stakeholder fits one of three roles in any given decision:

- **Decision-makers:** they pick. Their yes is the actual yes.
- **Influencers:** they don't pick, but the decision-maker checks with them. Their objection slows everything down.
- **Blockers:** they can't say yes, but they can stop the work. Procurement, legal, IT security.

data.title: The category trap
data.body: The same person is a decision-maker on one question and an influencer on another. Map by decision, not by name.

data.title: Power vs. Interest
data.body: The classic mapping. High power + high interest: manage closely. High power + low interest: keep satisfied. Low power + high interest: keep informed. Low power + low interest: monitor.

data.content:
The stakeholders who derail projects are usually the ones nobody put on the map. Three patterns to watch for:

- **The shadow approver.** Someone whose name doesn't appear in the org chart but whose blessing the decision-maker quietly seeks.
- **The historical defender.** They built the thing you're replacing. Their objection isn't the work — it's the legacy.
- **The cross-functional veto.** A team that doesn't own the decision but whose cooperation you need (Security, Compliance, Brand).

End-of-week deliverable: a one-pager naming every stakeholder, their role for *this* decision, their power/interest position, and the one thing they need from you to move forward.

The one-pager is the artifact you bring to your sponsor — it makes the work concrete and reveals who you've forgotten.
